title: Sennheiser Momentum 4 won't charge: troubleshooting
fault: Headphones do not charge when plugged in
diagnosis: Most often a bad cable, charger or dirty USB-C port is the cause, so I'll check those first, then look at a reset. If none of that works, the battery or main board may be at fault, which is a hard repair I'd send to Sennheiser service.
safety_notes: Unplug the cable before cleaning the port.
Never use metal tools inside the USB-C port.
Stop and do not charge if the cup is swollen, hot or smells odd.

steps.title: Unplug and power off
steps.instruction: Unplug any cable from the headphones and slide the power switch to off. Set them on a table with the right cup's bottom edge facing you.
steps.expected_visual_state: Headphones rest on a table with no cable attached and the status LED off.
common_mistakes: Cleaning the port while a cable is still connected

steps.title: Swap cable and charger
steps.instruction: Connect a different USB-C cable that you know works to a different wall adapter. Avoid laptop ports and wireless chargers for this test.
steps.expected_visual_state: A different cable is connected from a wall adapter to the headphones' USB-C port.
common_mistakes: Using a charge-only-damaged or frayed cable
Using a fast charger that outputs more than 5V without checking compatibility
Testing only from a weak laptop USB port

steps.title: Check the charging LED
steps.instruction: Watch the status LED for about a minute after plugging in. A pulsing LED means it is charging.
steps.expected_visual_state: The status LED on the right cup's bottom edge is lit or pulsing while the cable is connected.
common_mistakes: Giving up after only a few seconds
Expecting the LED to stay on a deeply drained battery right away

steps.title: Inspect the USB-C port
steps.instruction: Unplug the cable and shine a torch into the USB-C port on the right cup. Look for lint, dust or bent contacts.
steps.expected_visual_state: The USB-C port is visible in torchlight, showing whether lint or debris is packed inside.
common_mistakes: Not using enough light to see inside the port
Pressing on the port with a tool while looking

steps.title: Clean the port gently
steps.instruction: Use a wooden toothpick or plastic spudger to scrape out lint, moving along the port's flat side. Never use metal.
steps.expected_visual_state: The USB-C port is clear of lint and the center tongue is straight and undamaged.
common_mistakes: Using a metal pin that shorts or bends contacts
Digging hard and bending the center tongue
Blowing in the port with your mouth, adding moisture

steps.title: Reset the headphones
steps.instruction: Connect the cable, then hold the power switch toward Bluetooth for about 10 seconds to reset. Leave it charging for 15 minutes.
steps.expected_visual_state: Headphones sit connected to the cable with the LED showing charging activity.

steps.title: Test the charge
steps.instruction: After 15 minutes, switch the headphones on and check the battery level in the Sennheiser Smart Control app. If it has risen, the fault is fixed.
steps.expected_visual_state: The headphones are on with the LED lit and the phone app shows a battery level higher than before.
common_mistakes: Judging only from the LED color
Still using a bad cable for the final test
